summary: Jan Christian Schaffert works in Indology and computational fields. He studied at and held a post on the EdiKILex project at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, both attested in 2026.
Jan Dolensky is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, attested in 2013, studying under MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Jan E. M. Houben specializes in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at the Dutch Research Council (attested 1999) and Leiden University (attested 2000–2002), becoming Directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2003.

Jan Fontein worked in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (PhD under Theodoor Paul Galestin) and served as curator at the Rijksmuseum (1947, 1955) and Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1966–1992).

Jan Gonda was a Dutch scholar of Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University (PhD under Willem Caland) and Leiden University, subsequently serving at Utrecht University as Chair of Sanskrit (1929) and Indology professor (1932–1976).

Jan Hanusz was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig (~1880–1882) and completed his habilitation at Vienna (1884–1885). He studied under numerous scholars including Bühler, Müller, Brugmann, and Oldenberg, later teaching at Vienna (~1884–1887).

Jan Jakob Maria de Groot specialized in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Leiden University and under Georg von der Gabelentz, later serving as professor at Leiden University (1891–1912) and Professor of Sinology at Berlin (~1912–1921).

Jan Jaworski was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Warsaw (~1922–1927) and under Stanisław Schayer and Jean Przyluski, becoming a Privatdozent at Warsaw in 1930.

Jan Jetso Boeles specialized in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (1940–1945) under Nicolaas Johannes Krom and F. B. J. Kuiper, later serving as director of the Siam Society (~1959–1970).

Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak was a Sinologist who studied at Leiden (PhD), the Sorbonne, and Berlin, learning from Chavannes and Cordier. He spent his career at Leiden University (1919–1954), alongside guest professorships at Columbia, Princeton, and Oxford.
Jan Kornelis de Cock was an Indologist. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Amsterdam (~1895–1899), where he studied under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck.

Jan Laurens Andries Brandes specialized in Indology, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the Athenaeum Illustre and earned his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern, later serving as Keeper at the National Museum of Indonesia (~1884–1905).

Jan Michał Rozwadowski was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University (PhD) and Leipzig under Brugmann and Leskien. From 1897 he taught at Jagiellonian University, becoming Professor and Head of Comparative Linguistics in 1904.

Jan Mrázek works in linguistics, archaeology, and other fields. He completed his doctoral studies under Josef Zubatý (until 1925) and served as an Associate Professor at the National University of Singapore (attested 2011).

Jan N. Bremmer is a scholar of religious studies and history. He studied at VU Amsterdam, Bristol, and Amsterdam (PhD), later holding faculty posts at Utrecht University (1974–1990) and the University of Groningen (1990; 1996–2005).

Jan Nattier is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. She studied at Indiana and Harvard (PhD under Masatoshi Nagatomi), holding professorships at Macalester, Hawaii, Stanford, Indiana University Bloomington (1992–2005), and Soka University (2004–2010).

Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig. He held professorships at Saint Petersburg, Kazan, Tartu (1883–1893), Jagiellonian University (1893–1899), and the University of Warsaw (1918–1929).

Jan P. Hogendijk is an Indologist and historian. After receiving his doctorate from Utrecht University in 1983, he held posts at Brown, Frankfurt, Leiden (2004–2009), the University of Tehran, and Utrecht University (1986; professor 2005–2020).

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann works in Buddhist studies and related fields. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Marianne Pieper, and studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Rypka was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Vienna (~1905–1910), he held posts at Charles University in Prague (~1925–1958) and the University of Paris.
